# HPM 883 Computing Setup Guide

This guide walks you through setting up your computing environment for HPM 883. Complete these steps **before the first class** or during the first week.

::: {.callout-important}
## Required Accounts

You need:

1. **GitHub account** (with GitHub Education verified)
2. **Git** (for local development, optional)
3. **Positron or RStudio** (optional — Codespaces provides browser-based R)

**No local R installation required!** We use GitHub Codespaces which provides a complete R environment in your browser.
:::

---

## Step 1: Install R

### Windows

Open PowerShell and run:

```bash
winget install --id R-project.R
```

Or download from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/).

### macOS

Open Terminal and run:

```bash
brew install --cask r
```

Or download from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/).

### Verify Installation

Open a terminal and type:

```bash
R --version
```

You should see R version 4.3.0 or higher.

---

## Step 2: Install Positron (Recommended IDE)

**Positron** is Posit's new IDE with built-in AI assistance. It's free and actively developed.

### Download

1. Go to [positron.posit.co](https://positron.posit.co/)
2. Download the installer for your operating system
3. Run the installer

### Why Positron?

| Feature | Positron | RStudio |
|---------|----------|---------|
| Built-in AI assistant | ✓ Yes | No |
| VS Code extensions | ✓ 1000s | Limited |
| Active development | ✓ Very active | Maintenance only |
| Python support | First-class | Secondary |
| Price | Free | Free |

### Alternative: RStudio

If you prefer RStudio, download from [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).

---

## Step 3: Install Git and Create GitHub Account

### Install Git

**Windows:**

```bash
winget install Git.Git
```

**macOS:**

```bash
brew install git
```

### Configure Git

Open a terminal and run (use your actual name and email):

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "your.email@unc.edu"
```

### Create GitHub Account

1. Go to [github.com](https://github.com/)
2. Sign up with your UNC email (you get free Pro features as a student)
3. Verify your email address

### Connect Git to GitHub

Generate an SSH key (recommended):

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your.email@unc.edu"
```

Press Enter to accept defaults. Then add to GitHub:

1. Copy your public key: `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`
2. Go to GitHub → Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key
3. Paste and save

### Verify Connection

```bash
ssh -T git@github.com
```

You should see: "Hi username! You've successfully authenticated..."

---

## Step 4: Set Up GitHub Codespaces

GitHub Codespaces provides a browser-based R environment with zero local setup. This is our **primary computing environment** for labs and code-alongs.

### Verify GitHub Education

1. Go to [education.github.com/pack](https://education.github.com/pack)
2. Click "Get your Pack" and verify with your UNC email
3. This gives you **180 core-hours/month** of free Codespaces

::: {.callout-tip}
## Free for Students

GitHub Education provides free Codespaces access. No subscription required! You get:

- 180 core-hours/month (plenty for all coursework)
- 2-core or 4-core machines
- Pre-configured R environment with all packages
:::

### How Codespaces Works

When you accept a GitHub Classroom assignment:

1. Click the assignment link → Creates your personal repository
2. Click **"Open in Codespace"** → Browser-based RStudio launches
3. Complete your work in the browser
4. Commit and push when done — no file downloads needed

### Managing Codespaces

View and manage your Codespaces at [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces):

- **Stop** unused Codespaces to preserve hours
- **Delete** completed Codespaces to free quota
- **Rebuild** if environment issues occur

---

## Step 5: Install Quarto

Quarto is the publishing system we use for labs and the capstone project.

### Check if Already Installed

Positron and recent RStudio versions include Quarto. Check:

```bash
quarto --version
```

If not found, download from [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/).

---

## Step 6: Accept GitHub Classroom Assignment

Once the semester starts, you'll receive GitHub Classroom assignment links.

### How It Works

1. Click the assignment link (e.g., `https://classroom.github.com/a/xyz123`)
2. Authorize GitHub Classroom (first time only)
3. Accept the assignment → This creates your personal repository
4. Clone to your computer:

```bash
git clone git@github.com:unc-hpm-quant/lab-0-yourusername.git
```

5. Open the `.Rproj` file in Positron/RStudio

### First Time Setup (renv)

When you first open a project, restore packages:

```r
renv::restore()
```

This installs all required packages in the correct versions.

---

## Workflow Summary

### Labs & Code-Alongs (GitHub Codespaces — Primary)

1. Accept GitHub Classroom assignment (link in Canvas)
2. Click **"Open in Codespace"** → RStudio launches in browser
3. Complete the assignment in `analysis.qmd`
4. Render to HTML: `quarto render`
5. Commit and push from RStudio Git pane:
   ```bash
   git add .
   git commit -m "Complete Lab X"
   git push
   ```
6. Verify submission on GitHub

### Local Development (Optional)

For offline work or the capstone project:

1. Clone repository to local machine
2. Open in Positron/RStudio
3. Run `renv::restore()` (first time)
4. Complete the assignment
5. Render, commit, and push to GitHub

### Capstone Project

Works in Codespaces or locally. Uses extended template with:

- `targets` pipeline
- Pre-analysis plan
- Multi-file structure

---

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| `renv::restore()` fails | Delete `renv/library/`, restart R, try again |
| Package not found | Run `renv::install("package_name")` |
| Git push rejected | Run `git pull` first, then push |
| Quarto render fails | Check YAML header syntax |
| GitHub auth fails | Regenerate SSH key, re-add to GitHub |
| Codespaces slow | Stop unused Codespaces, use 4-core machine |
| Codespaces won't start | Check quota at [github.com/settings/billing](https://github.com/settings/billing) |
| "Open in Codespace" missing | Verify GitHub Education status |

### Getting Help

1. **Canvas Discussion Board** — Post questions, classmates can help
2. **Office Hours** — See course schedule
3. **GitHub Issues** — For persistent technical problems
